brief.notification_title: Relief bounce after rout; Dell and PCE are the tests
brief.market_summary: US futures are bouncing hard before the open: ES is at 7,101.50 (+2.4%) and NQ is up 3.2%. That follows the S&P 500's worst week since April 2025 (-8.61% to 6,910), which left all three indexes in correction, and VIX has eased to 31. Treasuries are giving back a little of last week's rally. The 10Y is at 4.932% (+2bp) after falling 18.9bp on the week, a 25bp December Fed hike is still priced, and the dollar index is above 104, its highest in 20 months. Brent shows $87.95 on the snapshot (-5%, though part of that is likely a contract roll) on surplus worries, despite Gulf shipping attacks and a Libyan outage. Crypto is barely joining in: BTC is $61,230 (+0.8%) after a $55.3k low on Saturday, the fear & greed index is at 11, and BTC ETFs lost $1.79B last week.
brief.since_last:
- **Futures turned up.** They rallied from +1.1% (S&P) at Sunday's open to about +2.4–2.6%. The trigger was Trump saying he hopes Nvidia's board rehires Jensen Huang; NVDA is about +6% pre-market, MU +4%, AMD +3% (n61, n26).
- **CrowdStrike reported and announced a deal.** EPS was $0.34 on revenue of $1.58B (+28%), and it raised FY27 EPS guidance to $1.28. It is also buying Zscaler in an all-stock deal worth about $43.9B. CRWD is about -8% and ZS about +14% (n64).
- **Health insurers are under pressure.** UNH, HUM and CVS slid after the US targeted Medicare Advantage ratings (n3).
- **Yields are up modestly as havens unwind.** The 10Y is +2bp and the 13-week bill is 4.143%. Markets have ruled out a 50bp hike in December but still expect 25bp (n62, n108).
- **Gold jumped 3.1% to $3,624.**
- **European flash PMIs missed.** Eurozone services came in at 51.2 vs 51.8 expected; UK services at 52.0 vs 52.5.
- **Brent slid.** Morning quotes were about $91–92, and the snapshot now shows $87.95. Goldman and Morgan Stanley have cut forecasts, but Libya lost about 350k bpd and Trump said strikes on Iran could resume after New Year (n145, n144, n138, n59).
- **BTC reclaimed $61k after Saturday's $55.3k low.** Strategy bought only 457 BTC (about $30M) while spending $212M buying back its own preferred shares (n14).
- **No US data has printed yet.** Flash PMIs are due at 09:45 ET.

economic_data.takeaway: Europe is softer, not collapsing (France services 46.6 vs 47.5). It adds to a slightly stronger dollar story against the euro, with no direct read for the Fed.
This is a five-month low. Like Europe, growth outside the US is cooling while the US runs hot, which helps keep the dollar index above 104.

economic_data.takeaway: Good news is bad news this week. A hot print adds to hike bets (n86), pushes the 2Y up before the 1pm auction and leans on the bounce. A miss helps both bonds and stocks.

economic_data.release: US S&P Global flash Services PMI (Nov)
economic_data.takeaway: Services drive US inflation. A print well above 55.6 supports the 'three hikes' camp (n120) and is a headwind for my IEF entry.
It's a secondary print, and it lands on the same morning as Best Buy and Dick's results. A drop after a $6T wealth hit (n75) would show the selloff feeding into spending.

This is the last inflation reading before the 9 Dec FOMC. A 0.3% or lower print keeps December at 25bp and lets duration work. A 0.4% print revives 50bp talk, lifts yields and the dollar, and is the 2022-style case where stocks and bonds fall together. It is my gate for IEF tranche 2.
Strong growth is already priced. An upside surprise together with firm core PCE is the hawkish combination.
The labour market is still tight. Only a jump well above 220K would change the Fed narrative.

FY27 EPS guidance raised to $1.28 from $1.25–1.26; Q4 guidance is EPS $0.36 on revenue of $1.638–1.644B. The all-stock Zscaler deal is worth about $43.9B, at 1.135 CRWD shares per ZS share.
earnings.takeaway: The stock is about -8% despite beating and raising. Holders are pricing dilution and integration risk, and the market is not paying up for tech beats. ZS is about +14%. It's a sector-level event for cybersecurity, not an index mover.
This is the first read on AI server demand this week and a warm-up for Dell. A miss on AI orders would hit SMH before Dell even reports.

The trigger is a Nvidia governance headline, not new fundamentals. Leadership is the same AI and crypto-linked names that led the selloff, while managed care is falling on Medicare Advantage scrutiny and CRWD is falling despite a beat.

UNH, HUM and CVS lower on Medicare Advantage ratings scrutiny. Morgan Stanley's Wilson calls the selloff a buying opportunity, while Goldman and BofA flag Fed risk (n18).

brief.instructor_take: My read: this is a relief rally, not a turn. Futures are up 2.4–3.2% because the S&P fell seven days in a row and Trump said he wants Jensen Huang back at Nvidia. That's a headline, not new earnings and not a change in the Fed's path. What drove the selloff is still in place: a December hike is priced, the dollar index is at a 20-month high above 104, and junk spreads just had their worst blowout of the year. The tell I'm watching is crypto. Bitcoin is up 0.8% while Nasdaq futures are up 3.2%, so speculative appetite isn't coming back with this bounce. The real tests come in two days: Dell after Tuesday's close (options imply about 15.7%) and core PCE on Wednesday at 08:30. Then the market goes quiet for Thanksgiving, and thin holiday trading can exaggerate whichever way those land. A less experienced investor tends to read the first gap-up after a 10% week as a signal. It usually isn't; the follow-through after the catalysts is what counts. So I'm not buying the open. I'd keep the bills, start a measured Treasury hedge while the 10Y is near 4.9%, and make semis prove themselves back above Thursday's level. If PCE prints 0.3% or lower and Dell gets bought, I'm happy to be a few percent late.

top_ideas.title: Keep T-bills as the core while the Fed hikes
top_ideas.one_liner: T-bills ~4.1-4.3% with a hike coming: keep cash in SGOV
top_ideas.thesis: The Fed is still expected to hike in December, so bill yields keep resetting higher: the 13-week is 4.143% and the official 3-month is 4.32%. That carry comes with almost no price risk while VIX is 31. SGOV is also the funding pool for the IEF tranches and any later semis rebuild.
top_ideas.reasoning: I start with the rate the Fed is actually moving, not the one I hope it moves. Markets have ruled out 50bp but still expect a quarter-point hike on 9 Dec (n62), and BNP sees policy going to 4.75% (n118). Each time bills roll, they roll into a higher yield; the 13-week is 4.143% today, up from 4.122% at the last brief. I earn that carry with almost no price risk, and that matters when the S&P just lost 8.6% in a week and VIX is still 31. I prefer SGOV to SHY because 1–3 year notes would lose some price if a hot PCE pushes the 2Y higher, for about the same yield. The second job of this position is optionality: holding dry powder lets me buy semis or duration on my terms instead of selling something at a bad price. I'd change my mind if the Fed blinks. If Williams tonight, or the data, signals December is the last hike or a pause, bill yields would drop below 4% and I'd move more into longer maturities. What newer investors miss is that cash here earns a positive real return; it isn't idle.

Core PCE and Q3 GDP, Wed 08:30 ET
risks: The Fed signals a pause after the equity rout, so reinvestment yields fall (lower income, not a capital loss)

top_ideas.entry: Keep the existing position and sweep idle cash into SGOV at market today. Draw on it to fund the IEF tranches (idea 3) and any later SMH rebuild.
top_ideas.invalidation: The 13-week yield (now 4.143%) falls below 4.0%, or Fed speakers signal December is the last hike or that a pause is coming.
top_ideas.sizing: Core cash reserve: about 15–20% of the portfolio while VIX is above 25

top_ideas.title: Avoid semis through Dell; don't chase the NVDA gap
top_ideas.one_liner: Semis gap up on a headline; wait for Dell and 2 closes >445
top_ideas.thesis: Semis took the worst of the selloff: SMH fell 10.6% on Friday and 17.8% on the week to 400.06. Today's bounce comes from a governance headline, not demand data. I'll buy back only after Dell is well received and SMH reclaims its pre-collapse level.
top_ideas.reasoning: Semis are where last week's damage concentrated. SMH lost 17.8% on the week against 8.6% for the S&P. This morning's bounce (NVDA about +6%, MU +4%, AMD +3%) comes from Trump hoping Nvidia's board rehires Jensen Huang. That changes neither AI capex nor the Fed's hiking path, and hikes hurt long-duration growth multiples most. My 445 trigger isn't arbitrary: it's roughly where SMH closed Thursday before Friday's -10.6%. Two closes above it would mean the market has fully rejected the breakdown. The evidence I want is Dell on Tuesday night, the cleanest read on AI server demand. HPE tonight and ADI before Tuesday's open come first. CrowdStrike is a useful warning: it beat on EPS ($0.34 vs $0.31 at one source) and raised guidance, yet it's about 8% lower, partly on its stock-funded Zscaler deal. The bar for tech to be rewarded is high right now. I'd rather pay 10% more after proof than catch a bounce that fails near Thursday's level. If SMH breaks below 400 after Dell, I extend the avoid into December.
catalysts: Dell results, Tue after close (implied move about 15.7%)
risks: The rebound is V-shaped and SMH runs above 445 before I re-enter, so I buy higher
A blowout Dell report, plus a reinstated Huang, flips sentiment quickly in thin holiday trading
top_ideas.entry: No new semis buying, including today's gap. After Dell: if Dell rose on its results and SMH closes above 445 on two straight sessions, buy half the previously trimmed amount from SGOV. Buy the second half after a further week above 445.
top_ideas.invalidation: Two consecutive SMH closes above 445 after a positively received Dell report end the avoid. A break below 400 after Dell extends the avoid into December.
top_ideas.sizing: 0% new semis exposure. Hold any remaining core position without adding.

top_ideas.title: Stage into 7-10Y Treasuries as an equity hedge
top_ideas.one_liner: 10Y at 4.93%: stage into IEF around PCE as an equity hedge
top_ideas.thesis: Last week Treasuries did their hedging job: the S&P fell 8.6% while IEF rose 1.79%. With the Fed hiking into tightening financial conditions, the 10Y near 4.9% pays well to hold a hedge. I'll buy in two tranches, using today's small backup in yields and Wednesday's PCE as the gate.
top_ideas.reasoning: The concept here is the stock-bond correlation. When growth fears drive the market, Treasuries rally as stocks fall, and that's exactly what happened last week: the 10Y fell 18.9bp, IEF rose 1.79% and TLT 2.61% while the S&P lost 8.6%. The Fed is hiking into junk spreads that just had their biggest blowout of 2026, and Ackman is warning of recession. The more the Fed tightens into that, the more likely it eventually has to reverse, which is what intermediate bonds price in. Today's +2bp backup as futures rally gives me a slightly better entry than Friday's close, and I'm paid about 4.9% to wait. I choose IEF over TLT because the 30Y at 5.3% carries more term-premium and supply risk from AI-related borrowing (n149) and swings far more. I choose it over more SGOV because bills don't rise when stocks fall. What would prove me wrong is inflation taking over: core PCE at 0.4% or higher would bring back the 2022 pattern, where stocks and bonds fall together. That's why tranche 2 waits for Wednesday. With IEF's duration of roughly 7 years, each 10bp move is about 0.7% in price, so size it as a hedge, not a bet.
catalysts: Core PCE, Q3 GDP and claims, Wed 08:30 ET
risks: Hot core PCE or PMIs drive yields and stocks lower together
Heavy auction supply and AI-related corporate issuance push up the term premium
The equity rebound extends and pulls the 10Y back above 5%
top_ideas.entry: Tranche 1 (1.5%): today after the 13:00 ET 2Y auction, if the 10Y is still at or above 4.90% (buy the backup, not a rally). Tranche 2 (1.5%): Wednesday after PCE, only if core is 0.3% m/m or lower. Fund both from SGOV.
top_ideas.invalidation: A 10Y close above 5.15% (roughly where last week began, and about a 1.5% drop in IEF), or core PCE at 0.4% m/m or higher.
top_ideas.sizing: 3% total, in two 1.5% tranches funded from SGOV

brief.prior_ideas_review:
1. **SGOV (add): worked; keep.** The 13-week yield went from 4.122% to 4.143%, so bills earned their carry while stocks corrected. Nothing has triggered the 4.0% or Fed-pause invalidation.

2. **SMH (avoid): worked; keep the rules unchanged.** SMH closed Friday at 400.06 (-10.6% on the day, -17.8% on the week), right on the 400 line. Today's NVDA-led gap-up doesn't change anything; Dell on Tuesday night is still the gate.

3. **XLV (staged buy): dropped before it triggered.** Tranche 1 was due Tuesday and nothing was bought. XLV held up on Friday (177.24, -0.12%). This morning, though, UNH, HUM and CVS are sliding as the US targets Medicare Advantage ratings (n3). Managed care is a meaningful part of XLV, and coming after a Democratic sweep of Congress (n45) it adds policy risk to a position that was meant to be ballast. I'm swapping that role to IEF, which actually rallied as stocks fell last week. Watch Medtronic Tuesday for information, but I wouldn't execute the XLV tranches.

lesson.explanation: Whether Treasuries hedge your stocks depends on what's scaring the market. When the fear is growth (earnings, a bubble deflating, recession), investors buy bonds as they sell stocks, so the two move in opposite directions and bonds cushion the portfolio. When the fear is inflation and a Fed forced to keep hiking, yields rise as stocks fall and both lose together, which is what happened in 2022. So a bond hedge is only as good as your read on which fear is in charge.
lesson.todays_example: Last week growth fear dominated: the S&P fell 8.61% while the 10Y dropped 18.9bp and IEF gained 1.79%. This morning the see-saw is running in reverse, with futures up 2.4% and yields up 2bp. Wednesday's core PCE decides which regime we're in. A print of 0.3% or lower keeps the hedge working; 0.4% or higher risks the 2022 pattern, which is why IEF tranche 2 waits for it.
